Name: Salawara Estate - Red Honey - Sakleshpur - Light Roast
Tasting_Notes: Blackberries, Orange Zest and a lingering sugarcane sweetness
Desc:
Elevation: 1100 MASL  
  Variety: S795  
  Processing: Red Honey  
  Fermentation: 72 hours Anaerobic fermentation  
  Roast: Light  
  Producers: Sharan Gowda  
    Tasting notes: Amla, Kinnow & Jaggery  
 As many of you might know, Sharan was one of the first farmers we ever bought coffee from, in fact he was the first planter we ever met in real life! Back then Salawara Estate was just starting their speciality coffee journey, but in the last five years, they have undoubtedly emerged as one of the most outstanding coffee producers in the country. Their steadfast focus on agriculture and improving their infrastructure rather than content creation has yielded incredible results, and we're the ones reaping the benefits! 
 This year we purchased four lots from them, but this Anaerobic Red Honey was by far our favourite when we cupped it, and with the final roast profile, it's one of the juiciest coffees we have tasted in a while! This S795 grown at 1100 MASL was the last batch of coffee that was processed last year, and the slow maturation, with a higher mucilage content made this the perfect bunch for an Anerobic Red Honey Process. The Cherries were pulped lightly, leaving a lot of the mucilage and were then fermented Anaerobically for 72 hours before they were slow dried for 22 days. The cherries and the process produced a very fruit forward cup, high in sweetness and acidity. 
 To accentuate this, we roasted this super light, and the result is a super juicy coffee with notes of Blackberries, Orange Zest and a lingering sugarcane sweetness.

Name: Salawara Estate - Red Honey - Sakleshpur - Light Roast
Tasting_Notes: Blackberries, Orange Zest and a lingering sugarcane sweetness
Desc:
Elevation: 1100 MASL  
  Variety: S795  
  Processing: Red Honey  
  Fermentation: 72 hours Anaerobic fermentation  
  Roast: Light  
  Producers: Sharan Gowda  
    Tasting notes: Amla, Kinnow & Jaggery  
 As many of you might know, Sharan was one of the first farmers we ever bought coffee from, in fact he was the first planter we ever met in real life! Back then Salawara Estate was just starting their speciality coffee journey, but in the last five years, they have undoubtedly emerged as one of the most outstanding coffee producers in the country. Their steadfast focus on agriculture and improving their infrastructure rather than content creation has yielded incredible results, and we're the ones reaping the benefits! 
 This year we purchased four lots from them, but this Anaerobic Red Honey was by far our favourite when we cupped it, and with the final roast profile, it's one of the juiciest coffees we have tasted in a while! This S795 grown at 1100 MASL was the last batch of coffee that was processed last year, and the slow maturation, with a higher mucilage content made this the perfect bunch for an Anerobic Red Honey Process. The Cherries were pulped lightly, leaving a lot of the mucilage and were then fermented Anaerobically for 72 hours before they were slow dried for 22 days. The cherries and the process produced a very fruit forward cup, high in sweetness and acidity. 
 To accentuate this, we roasted this super light, and the result is a super juicy coffee with notes of Blackberries, Orange Zest and a lingering sugarcane sweetness.

Name: Winter Blend
Tasting_Notes: cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste
Desc:
Meet the blend our roasters look forward to crafting each winter. Pairing well with milk, it is also a solid base for all those winter recipes you've been saving. 
 We've created it using a careful mix of natural and washed lots from St. Joseph Estate and Attikan Estate. Opening with the aroma of brown spices, this coffee has a medium body and a syrupy, round mouthfeel. You’ll be able to taste cinnamon, cacao, roasted almonds, and raisins, and tying everything together nicely is a chocolatey aftertaste. 
 We recommend brewing it as an espresso, or with a Moka Pot or French Press. 
  Recommended Resting Period:  10 Days

Name: Half - Caff
Tasting_Notes: roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish
Desc:
Our first-ever single-origin, specialty Half-Caff comes from Yelnoorkhan Estate. We selected their S795, washed processed coffee to create a complex and distinctive cup.   
 To reduce caffeine by 55%, we used CO₂ decaffeination, a chemical-free, minimal-waste generating method that is conscious in its water and energy usage. We chose it because the other decaffeination methods available to us in India came with a catch. In removing all the caffeine, they also took away the depth that makes a cup memorable. Adding artificial flavours was not something we wanted to do, never mind the fact that many of these methods also used far too much water.   
 The result is a cup with a gentler kick that holds its own in terms of flavour. You’ll first notice chocolate biscuits on the nose as well as your palate. A silky mouthfeel then reveals notes of roasted hazelnuts and malt, followed by a long, nutty finish.  
 For the best experience, brew this coffee using an espresso machine. It tastes great black and is equally suited to milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    5    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Krishnagiri Estate
Tasting_Notes: oak, toasted walnuts, and malt
Desc:
A single origin dark roast, this coffee comes from a Rainforest Alliance Certified farm. The producers used a custom-designed pulper to process this washed lot, minimising water usage.   
 In the cup, you'll first notice the aroma of brown spices. The brew, characterised by mellow acidity, a heavy body, and a velvety mouthfeel, reminds of oak, toasted walnuts, and malt. A bittersweet finish lingers between sips.   
 We recommend brewing this coffee as an espresso, using a Moka Pot, French Press, or an AeroPress. It is rich enough to enjoy black, and also pairs well with milk. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    7  Days

Name: Monsoon Malabar AA- Hoysala Estate
Tasting_Notes: cocoa nib s and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate
Desc:
We’re excited to bring back Monsoon Malabar from Hoysala Estate. The unique flavour profile of this coffee develops when winds and humidity from seasonal monsoon rain change the characteristics of the  coffee beans . While this process has its accidental roots in colonial India when a shipment to Europe was attacked by the full force of monsoon winds, similar conditions have been recreated in a controlled environment for consistency in every lot produced.  
 When roasted medium dark, the result is a medium-bodied cup that invites with sweet aromas of butter biscuits, treating you to notes of  cocoa nib s and dried fruit, concluding with the aftertaste of dark chocolate. Best enjoyed when brewed as an espresso, in the Moka Pot or the French press, the nutty flavour profile of this coffee makes for a delicious cup, either milky or black.  
  Recommended Resting Period:     15 Days

Name: Dhak Blend
Tasting_Notes: dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste
Desc:
Our  Dhak Blend  is an ode to one of our favorite Indian trees with its colorful flame-like flowers that signal the onset of Spring. The coffees used in this blend are naturally processed which means that the  coffee beans  are dried with the cherry, resulting in complex, fruity and sweet flavours. 
 Roasted dark to bring out flavours of dark chocolate and fruit jam, this blend's heavy cocoa body leaves a smooth lingering aftertaste. 
 Our roasting team recommends the Dhak Blend for espresso-based drinks as well as manual brews such as the Moka Pot and the French Press.

Name: Attikan Estate
Tasting_Notes: At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.
Desc:
Attikan Estate's arabica  coffee beans  come from the Biligiriranga Hills in Karnataka and is make for one of our most popular coffees. Sweet with fruity overtones and balanced acidity, this is the darkest of our standard medium roasts and recommended for espresso lovers. It is a versatile coffee that also works for manual brewing such as Moka Pot, South Indian Filter and AeroPress.  
 Located to the south of Mysore, the Biligiriranga Hills, or ‘white hills’ are named after the mist that hangs over the region. At 1650 meters, it is amongst the highest coffee growing regions in India and grows Selection 9, Selection 795, Cauvery and Kent varieties of Arabica, along with Silver Oaks, citrus, and fig trees.

Name: Basankhan Estate
Tasting_Notes: In addition to coffee, the estate cultivates other crops such as black pepper, oranges, cardamom, lemons, and bananas.
Desc:
We are thrilled to present our first ever single origin dark roast, with  coffee beans  sourced from a new partner farm— Estate in Chikmagalur, Karnataka.  
 This coffee has a journey of rich, complex flavours that will leave you craving for more. As you take a sip, enjoy the velvety mouthfeel reminiscent of dark chocolate, which enhances the overall richness of this brew. The coffee’s body is heavy and round, creating a luscious and full-bodied experience that envelops your palate. If you’ve liked our dark roasts like  Vienna  and  Dhak , you’ll love this one!  The Basankhan Estate is a family-owned farm located in Chikmagalur, Karnataka with a rich history spanning over 100 years. In addition to coffee, the estate cultivates other crops such as black pepper, oranges, cardamom, lemons, and bananas.

Desc:

Name: Mooleh Manay Estate – CM Natural
Tasting_Notes: fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness
Desc:
Returning to our Producer Series after 2023, Komal Sable and Akshay Dashrath share their first experiment with carbonic maceration. Building on the clarity and consistency they achieved with anaerobic fermentation last season, the fifth-generation producers modified their drums to create a CO₂-rich, oxygen-free environment that allows for slower, more controlled fermentation within whole cherries.  
 The process began by removing floaters to select only ripe, dense cherries, followed by a brief pre-drying phase to reduce surface moisture. The cherries were then sealed in drums, and a custom culture was introduced to extend the fermentation. Over 60 hours, this combination of carbonic maceration and yeast inoculation ensured thorough mucilage breakdown and the development of deep complexity.  
 Post-fermentation, the cherries were dried on raised beds inside a polyhouse. Continuous raking over 7 to 10 days ensured even drying until a final moisture level of 11–12% was reached.  
 Roasted light by Rishab from our team, this coffee offers a well-structured cup with notes of fermented red fruit and a bright, juicy sweetness. It opens with the aroma of mixed berries and carries a syrupy mouthfeel, with layered flavours of dried fig, plum, black grape, and mulberry. A chocolatey aftertaste marks the finish, adding further depth.  
 We recommend brewing this expressive coffee black, as a Pour Over, or using an AeroPress. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    16  Days

Name: 13th Birthday Blend
Tasting_Notes: strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries
Desc:
This celebratory blend brings together natural lots from Stanmore, Orchardale, and Riverdale Estates in Yercaud, along with a washed lot from Unakki Estate in Chikmagalur, which forms the base. Its flavour profile takes us back to the Black Forest cakes many of us celebrated birthdays with during our teen years.  
 Opening with the aroma of honey and strawberries, the cup has a medium-high body and a round mouthfeel. You'll notice notes of strawberry, chocolate, cherry, and pear, followed by a lingering finish of chocolate-covered strawberries.  
 This blend brews well across a range of methods, including espresso, AeroPress, French Press, Moka Pot, and Pour Over. Equally enjoyable black or with milk, it lends itself to a wide range of recipes. 
   Recommended Resting Period:     10   Days

Name: SKIA Coffee (Pack of 2)
Tasting_Notes: sweet lime, prunes, and almond
Desc:
This two-pack (100 gms each) brings together distinct coffees from Nelaji Village in Coorg. Grown by smallholder farmers and processed by Ashish Rao, a first-generation producer, these lots mark our first collaboration with Skia Coffee.  
 Ripe, high-density cherries were pulped with the mucilage left intact, then placed in sealed tanks for a 72-hour anaerobic fermentation. A yeast strain purpose-built for controlled fermentation was introduced during this stage to develop complexity.  
 From there, the two lots took separate paths.  
  Honey Sun Dried    
 The first lot was dried slowly on raised beds under controlled shade. Roasted to a medium profile, it makes for a balanced cup with notes of sweet lime, prunes, and almond.  
  Recommended Resting Period:  16 Days 
  Thermal Shock    
 This second lot was immersed in hot water, then rapidly cooled in ice. It was then mechanically washed and dried slowly under shade. Also roasted to a medium profile, it brews cups with notes of tangerine, brown sugar, and berries.   
 Both coffees brew beautifully as an espresso or with an AeroPress, Moka Pot, or French Press. They taste great black and pair well with milk. Together, they offer a chance to explore how thoughtful shifts in processing shape flavour in the final cup.   
  Recommended Resting Period:  12 Days

Name: Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective
Tasting_Notes: blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish
Desc:
It's always exciting for us to partner with a new farm. With Meghalaya's Warsanlyngdoh Coffee Collective, that excitement runs even deeper. A completely new coffee growing region for us, it speaks of the possibilities that the North East Indian soil holds for specialty production. The collective’s origin goes back a decade, when Daman, a first-generation coffee producer, visited Nongryniang—a remote village in Khasi Hills and home to the nanny who cared for him in his early years.  
 " There, nestled among the misty hills, I came across two old coffee plants growing in someone’s backyard. I later learned that back in the 1980s, the government had briefly launched a coffee planting program in the area. Like many such initiatives, it had long been abandoned and forgotten. But those plants stayed with me. And so did the people .", he recounts. Since then, Daman started a decade-long pursuit of craft and community. From shading systems to post-harvest processing, he spent years learning all it takes to grow high-quality coffee. Over time, the collective has grown in both, resolve and numbers, with 75 farmers now contributing to a harvest. They pick only the ripest cherries by hand, which are sun-dried for 15–22 days depending on weather conditions.   
 The first coffee that we’ve sourced from the collective is a natural lot we’ve chosen to roast to a medium profile. It brews cups that open with the aroma of raisins, unfolding into a creamy mouthfeel. Notes of blueberry, black tea, and khasi mandarin carry through in each sip, with a long, marmalade-like finish. A balanced coffee, it lends well to various brewing methods, including espresso, Moka Pot, French Press, and AeroPress. It is enjoyable on its own as well as in milk-based beverages. 
  Recommended Resting Period:    13  Days

Name: Ratnagiri Estate - Dark Room Natural
Tasting_Notes: passionfruit, mosambi, pineapple, and black tea follow, with the tea-like note carrying through the finish
Desc:
Our latest release from Ratnagiri Estate showcases a new frontier in controlled processing. It was shaped by a 60-hour fermentation with a custom culture, then dried slowly for 13 days in the estate’s climate-controlled dark room. 
 A rare facility found at only a handful of estates worldwide, the dark room is fully sealed and fitted with precision racks. It holds temperature between 2°C and 30°C and maintains humidity at 10%. Slow drying with this level of control deepens flavour, preserves sweetness, and brings clarity to the cup. 
 Antony, our roaster, approached the roast with a carefully extended Maillard phase to build natural sweetness, finishing light to let the coffee’s character shine. The result is a sparkling wine-like cup with a silky body and a bright mouthfeel. It opens with the aroma of strawberry and prune. Notes of passionfruit, mosambi, pineapple, and black tea follow, with the tea-like note carrying through the finish. 
 For the best experience, we suggest brewing this limited-edition lot as a Pour Over or using an AeroPress. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    8    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Kalledevarapura Estate - The Fermentation Edit
Tasting_Notes: plum, raw mango, candy apple, and goji berries
Desc:
Meet our roasters’ favourite experiment from Nano-X ’25. 
 To create this special five-pack, we played with a whole spectrum of microorganisms, from homegrown kombucha to lab-cultured strains. Working with a local laboratory, the producer, Shravan, curated a diverse range of cultures, while Tyler, our Head of Roastery, prepared a robust batch of active kombucha using black tea and raw sugar. 
 Ripe coffee cherries were split into eleven barrels of 120 kg each, with inoculants gradually added to ten barrels while one was kept as a control. The barrels were sealed and left indoors for a 72-hour fermentation, with the kombucha batch opened after 24 hours to allow oxygen exposure, as the SCOBY (Symbiotic Culture of Bacteria and Yeast) requires it to remain active. Once fermentation was complete, the cherries were dried on raised beds for 20 to 25 days. 
 This limited-release brings together the highest-scoring samples from the experiment. It includes lots fermented with: 
 Homegrown Kombucha, creating a cup with notes of plum, raw mango, candy apple, and goji berries. 
 Saccharomyces cerevisiae, building an expressive coffee with notes of white nectarine, pomegranate, roasted hazelnut, and pomelo. 
 Pichia yeast, developing a clean cup with notes of cane sugar, green apple, jaggery, and roasted almonds. 
 Lactic acid bacteria, which shaped a coffee with notes of orange zest, black raisin, wild honey, and cocoa. 
 An anaerobically processed natural, used to benchmark the inoculated lots. It brews cups with hints of florality and notes of lemonade, roasted almond, and green grape. 
 We recommend drinking these coffees black, brewed as Pour Overs or using the AeroPress. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    12    Days  
   Note:    This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Name: Riverdale Estate - White Rose
Tasting_Notes: plum, pomegranate, strawberry and orange blossom, complemented by a smooth mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness
Desc:
Fermented with rose petals, this layered light roast perfectly embodies why Riverdale Estate is a pioneer in experimental processing. 
 Only the ripest cherries, hand-picked from the higher-altitude blocks of the farm, where the fruit matures slowly and develops an enhanced sweetness, were used. Once harvested, the cherries underwent a triple wash with natural spring water to remove impurities. 
 After removing floaters, rose petals were introduced during fermentation, setting up the stage for complexity. The cherries were then slow-dried on raised beds for up to 30 days, allowing for even drying. Finally, the coffee was hulled at the estate’s dry mill, where any defective beans were eliminated before being sent to our roastery. 
 The result is a gently perfumed cup with bright notes of plum, pomegranate, strawberry and orange blossom, complemented by a smooth mouthfeel and a lingering sweetness. 
 We recommend brewing it black using an AeroPress or as a Pour Over. 
   Recommended Resting Period:    14  Days  
     Note:  This coffee pack is a special release with limited availability and, therefore, cannot be included in a subscription plan.

Desc:
Meet our second release by Amruthavarshini Estate, a women-led estate run by a mother-daughter duo. Processed using the anaerobic natural method, this medium roast brews fruity and nutty cups with a pleasant sweetness.   
 A honey-like aroma leads into bright notes of cherries and pineapples. The nuttiness of roasted almonds adds depth, while the mouthfeel remains syrupy. In the finish, you’ll taste the lingering aftertaste of raisins and nuts.

Name: Breakfast Blend - Medium Roast - Stoned fruits with caramel overtones
Tasting_Notes: Stoned Fruits and Caramel overtones giving a balanced mouthfeel and texture to the final cup
Desc:

  We recommend this elegant & refreshing coffee as the first cup in the morning & so we named it as the “Breakfast Blend”.

Name: Liquid Gold - Aura estate
Tasting_Notes: Figs • Strawberry • Peaches
Desc:
Aura Farming – Dry Osmosis Process Method. Grown at 3700ft above sea level, Liquid Gold is crafted from Coffee cherries harvested at a ripeness level of above 95%. After harvesting, the cherries are washed, and all floating fruits are removed to ensure quality selection. The coffee cherries are taken to raised beds for drying and dried until it reaches 45% moisture. The cherries are then transferred to a container and fermented anaerobically for 48 hours. After fermentation, they are moved to raised beds and dried slowly for 25 days. During the drying period, temperature and relative humidity are carefully monitored and maintained to ensure uniform drying and preserve coffee quality.  
  Tasting Notes:   
  Figs • Strawberry • Peaches

Name: Ratnagiri Estate: Jasmine Kissed Cranberry
Tasting_Notes: Grapefruit, Pomegranate, Rose
Desc:
Jasmine kissed cranberry - 100 % arabica that is sourced from  Chikmagalur, grown at an altitude of approximately 4,100ft to 4,500ft. It gets its unique name through a process which include a strain of yeast used to create a carbon dioxide-rich environment during fermentation in stainless-steel fermenters. A remarkable level of complexity in the beans is created by this process, laying the groundwork for a wonderful cup of coffee. Steady drying on raised beds is the next important step, which lets the flavors gradually develop and intensify. After another 30 days of continuous stirring, the coffee undergoes additional drying developing  scent of jasmine, complex notes of raspberries, cranberries, and sparkling malic acidity with a lingering floral aftertaste. 
 Tasting Notes: Grapefruit, Pomegranate, Rose

Name: COZY COOKIE
Tasting_Notes: Thick, creamy, and dessert-like, supported by malted vanilla notes and a smooth, lingering finish.
Desc:
Cozy Cookie  
 A washed coffee from Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia, roasted as a balanced omni roast for both filter and espresso. 
  Cozy Cookie  is warm, smooth, and comforting by design. Built around sweetness and body rather than acidity, it brings together cocoa, nuts, and soft vanilla notes in a cup that feels familiar and easy. It’s gentle without being boring, sweet without being heavy. 
 
  Taste Profile  
  Filter  
 Cocoa and roasted nuts lead the cup, followed by soft vanilla sweetness. The profile stays round and smooth with low acidity, finishing clean and cozy with a lingering chocolatey warmth. 
  Espresso  
 Caramel cookie sweetness with a chocolate-forward body. Thick, creamy, and dessert-like, supported by malted vanilla notes and a smooth, lingering finish. Especially good with milk. 
 
  Brew Recipes  
  V60  
 Coffee: 15 g Water: 240 ml Ratio: 1:16 Temperature: 92–94°C Grind: Medium Brew Time: 2:30–3:00 
 Results in a smooth, cocoa-driven cup with gentle sweetness and a calm, comforting finish. 
  Espresso  
 Dose: 18 g Yield: 38–40 g Time: 28–32 seconds Ratio: ~1:2.1 
 Creamy, chocolatey espresso with caramel cookie sweetness and a rounded mouthfeel. 
 
  Details  
 Origin: Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia Varietal: Mixed Heirloom Process: Washed Roast: Medium Omni Brew: Filter & Espresso

Name: DARK HONEY
Tasting_Notes: Honeyed Apricot · Dried Figs · Wildflower Nectar
Desc:
Chikmagalur, KA | SLN 795 | Dark Honey Process | 100% Arabica  
 This one’s for those who chase depth. 
 Sourced from the lush slopes of Unnaki Estate, this Arabica is processed using the Dark Honey method where part of the mucilage is left intact during drying, letting natural sugars soak into the bean. What you get is a cup bursting with golden complexity. 
 Think: honeyed apricot, dried figs, and a soft wildflower nectar finish. 
 Roasted medium to keep the balance between fruit and body. Smooth acidity, full texture, and a lingering sweetness that doesn’t quit. 
  Tasting Notes:  Honeyed Apricot · Dried Figs · Wildflower Nectar 
  Elevation:  4000–4700 FT  Process:  Dark Honey  Roast Level:  Medium  Varietal:  SLN 795

Name: HARBOR MALABAR
Tasting_Notes: Taste Notes Cocoa Nibs, Nutty, Raisins - with an mellow sweet finish Roast Medium-Dark Variety SLN 795 Process Monsooning Region Chikkamagalur, Karnataka Elevation 1200 MSL
Desc:
A slow aged coffee shaped by India’s monsoon winds, this Arabica from Chikkamagalur goes through the traditional monsooning process where the beans swell, mellow, and transform in both color and character. The result is a cup that’s incredibly smooth, almost zero in acidity, and deeply grounding. 
 It opens with earthy and woody tones, followed by a soft musty depth that’s unique to monsooned coffees. The finish is mellow, slightly sweet, and comforting in a way only this style can deliver a warm, rugged, and unmistakably Indian. 
  Taste Notes  Cocoa Nibs, Nutty, Raisins - with an mellow sweet finish 
  Roast  Medium-Dark 
  Variety  SLN 795 
  Process  Monsooning 
  Region  Chikkamagalur, Karnataka 
  Elevation  1200 MSL

Name: HOUSE NO. 02
Tasting_Notes: Warm Cocoa • Brown Sugar • A Familiar Finish A balanced, full-bodied espresso blend designed for everyday comfort.
Desc:
Warm Cocoa • Brown Sugar • A Familiar Finish A balanced, full-bodied espresso blend designed for everyday comfort. 
 House No. 02 is the second release in our House Series — a lineup of coffees built around routine, consistency, and quiet familiarity. 
 Built on a washed base from Chikamagalur, layered with arabica cherry for body, and finished with a touch of natural sweetness from Kaimara, this blend is smooth, rounded, and deeply satisfying. 
 Expect a cup that leans into warmth soft cocoa notes, gentle brown sugar sweetness, and a full, comforting body that holds beautifully across brew styles. It’s easy to drink, easy to dial in, and hard to replace once you get used to it. 
 Designed for everyday use, House No. 02 performs just as well with milk as it does black. Whether it’s your morning espresso or an evening cup, this is the kind of coffee you reach for without thinking. 
 
  The House Series  
 House No. 02 continues our House Series, coffees designed to be part of your everyday. 
 Every fourth drop introduces a new House blend. Not one-offs, but evolving expressions of what a daily coffee can be. 
 House No. 01 set the foundation. House No. 02 builds on it, fuller, smoother, more refined. 
 With House No. 03, 04 and beyond, the idea remains the same: different expressions, same purpose. 
 Built to stay. Refined over time. 
 
  Why you’ll love it  
 • Smooth, full-bodied cup with low to medium acidity • Warm cocoa profile with a soft, natural sweetness • Excellent crema and texture for espresso • Works beautifully with milk and black brews • Balanced and easy to dial in across methods 
 
  Brew Guide  
 Works best for: 
 Espresso Moka Pot French Press South Indian Filter Manual Pour Over (for a fuller, richer cup) 
 
  Roast Level  
 Medium to Medium Dark Roast 
 
  Who is this for?  
 If you enjoy balanced coffees with a warm, chocolate-forward profile and a smooth, comforting finish—House No. 02 is built for your everyday. 
 
  Freshly Roasted  
 Roasted in small batches at our Delhi roastery and shipped fresh. 
 
  Some coffees come and go. This one stays.

 Built to stay. Refined over time.

Name: MOJITO
Tasting_Notes: What this really means is flavor with layers: cocoa and raisin at the core, a lift of sweet lime, and a finish that hints at cacao nib and dried dates.
Desc:
This lot from Melkodige Estate is our kind of experiment done right. Ripe SL9 cherries were hand-picked, floated to remove lights, then submerged with EM5 microbes for a 74-hour anaerobic ferment. After that, the cherries were moved to raised wooden trays and dried under shade for 15 days. 
 What this really means is flavor with layers: cocoa and raisin at the core, a lift of sweet lime, and a finish that hints at cacao nib and dried dates. It’s juicy without getting wild, sweet without tasting candy-like. 
 We roast this medium-light to keep the lime sparkle and retain the chocolatey depth that makes the cup feel complete. If you’re into expressive naturals that still behave well on brew bar, this is the one. 
 Taste 
 Cocoa, raisin, sweet lime, cacao nib, dried dates. 
 Brew guide 
 
 
 Filter: 1:16, 92–94°C, 2:45–3:00 total (V60/Kalita/AeroPress). 
 
 
 Light espresso: 1:2.3 in 30–34s; expect a syrupy shot with citrus pop. 
 
 
 Specs 
 
 
 Estate: Melkodige Estate, Chikmagalur, KA 
 
 
 Variety: SL9 
 
 
 Process: EM5 anaerobic natural (74-hour submerged ferment) 
 
 
 Drying: 15 days on raised, shaded beds 
 
 
 Elevation: 4200 ft MSL 
 
 
 Roast: Medium-Light 
 
 
 Best for: Filter, pourover, AeroPress; adventurous light espresso 
 
 
 Freshness: Roasted to order. Peak from day 7–28. Reseal tight.

Name: ANAEROBIC NATURALS- AMMIKULAVI ESTATE
Tasting_Notes: PLUM CAKE, LEMON VERBENA, SPICE, STRAWBERRY, CACAO NIBS Best Brewed with: POUR-OVER, AEROPRESS, OR MODERN ESPRESSO
Desc:
FROM THE COOL, ELEVATED LANDSCAPE OF THE PULNEY HILLS IN TAMIL NADU COMES A COFFEE SHAPED BY CAREFUL HANDWORK, CONTROLLED FERMENTATION, AND TIME. THIS IS OUR FIRST COLLABORATION WITH THE AMMIKULAVI ESTATE, LOCATED NEAR KODAIKANAL AT AROUND 1400 MASL, WHERE SLOW CHERRY DEVELOPMENT AND COOL CLIMATES ALLOW FLAVOUR TO FORM WITH DEPTH AND STRUCTURE. 
 THIS MICROL0T IS PRODUCED USING A 72-HOUR ANAEROBIC FERMENTATION, WHERE RIPE, HAND-PICKED CHERRIES ARE SEALED IN AIRTIGHT BARRELS TO DEVELOP SWEETNESS AND COMPLEXITY IN A CONTROLLED, OXYGEN-FREE ENVIRONMENT. FOLLOWING FERMENTATION, THE COFFEE IS WASHED, BRIEFLY SUN-DRIED, AND THEN SHADE-DRIED SLOWLY ON RAISED BEDS. A FINAL RESTING PERIOD ALLOWS THE FLAVOURS TO STABILISE AND INTEGRATE FULLY. 
 IN THE CUP, THIS COFFEE IS LAYERED AND EXPRESSIVE, WITH NOTES OF PLUM CAKE, LEMON VERBENA, WARM SPICE, STRAWBERRY, AND CACAO NIBS. ROASTED MEDIUM-LIGHT, IT MAINTAINS CLARITY AND SWEETNESS WHILE OFFERING A ROUNDED BODY AND STRUCTURED FINISH. 
 THIS IS A COFFEE THAT REFLECTS ITS PROCESS AND PLACE HONESTLY — PATIENT, BALANCED, AND QUIETLY COMPLEX.  
   Information:  
  Estate:  THE AMMIKULAVI ESTATE 
  Region:  PULNEY HILLS, TAMIL NADU 
  Elevation:  1400 MASL 
  Varietal:  CATURRA, S795, S9 
  Lot:  MICROLOT 
  Process:  72-HOUR ANAEROBIC NATURALS 
  Roast Level:  MEDIUM-LIGHT

From the high-altitude slopes of Attikan Estate comes an   exclusive natural microlot   that’s as expressive as it is elegant. The natural process brings out a   vivid fruit-forward character  , and we knew the roast had to preserve every layer of its complexity.

Name: CHINA YUNNAN — NATURAL DOUBLE FERMENTATION
Tasting_Notes: MANDARIN, GREEN APPLE, TEA-LIKE, PEACH Best Brewed With: Espresso, Aeropress, Pour Over
Desc:
Information:    
 FROM THE HIGH-ALTITUDE REGIONS OF YUNNAN, CHINA, COMES A COFFEE THAT STOOD OUT TO US FOR ITS CLARITY AND STRUCTURE. GROWN IN MENGLIAN, PU’ER, AT 1300–1600 MASL, THIS REGION’S SUBTROPICAL CLIMATE AND ELEVATION SHIFTS ALLOW FLAVOURS TO DEVELOP SLOWLY AND WITH PRECISION. 
 WHAT DREW US TO THIS LOT WAS ITS BALANCE — A NATURAL DOUBLE FERMENTATION THAT ADDS DEPTH WITHOUT OVERWHELMING THE CUP. THROUGH A CAREFULLY CONTROLLED EXTENDED FERMENTATION, THE COFFEE DEVELOPS LAYERED COMPLEXITY WHILE RETAINING A CLEAN, TEA-LIKE QUALITY. 
 WE ROASTED THIS COFFEE LIGHT TO PRESERVE ITS STRUCTURE AND BRIGHTNESS, KEEPING THE ACIDITY LIFTED AND THE FINISH REFINED. THE IDEA WAS SIMPLE — LET THE COFFEE STAY TRANSPARENT, AND LET ITS CHARACTER COME THROUGH. 
 IN THE CUP, EXPECT MANDARIN AND GREEN APPLE BRIGHTNESS, A SOFT PEACH-LIKE SWEETNESS, AND A DISTINCT TEA-LIKE QUALITY THAT MAKES THIS COFFEE FEEL LIGHT, ELEGANT, AND EASY TO RETURN TO.

Desc:
FROM THE HILLS OF VALLE DEL CAUCA IN COLOMBIA COMES A COFFEE THAT IMMEDIATELY STOOD OUT FOR ITS INTENSITY AND FRUIT EXPRESSION. INMACULADA IS KNOWN FOR PUSHING BOUNDARIES IN PROCESSING, AND THIS LOT REFLECTS THAT APPROACH — PRECISE, EXPERIMENTAL, AND BUILT AROUND FLAVOUR.

Name: Honey Double Fermentation
Tasting_Notes: Initially, the coffee cherries are fermented whole without depulping, allowing the fruit to impart rich, fruity flavors and aromas.
Desc:
This beautiful microlot coffee from Baarbara Estate undergoes a distinctive double fermentation process, combining the benefits of natural and honey processing methods. Initially, the coffee cherries are fermented whole without depulping, allowing the fruit to impart rich, fruity flavors and aromas. After this natural fermentation stage, the pulp is removed, and the coffee undergoes a secondary fermentation with a layer of mucilage intact, characteristic of the honey process. This innovative approach enhances the coffee's complexity, sweetness, and body, resulting in a truly unique flavor profile that showcases the best of both processing worlds.   
   Information:

  Region:  Chikmagalur, Karnataka

Desc:

Name: Tricolate Coffee Brewer
Desc:
The Right Conditions for High Extractions 
 Taking inspiration from precision pouring accessories and flat-bed brewers alike, the Tricolate offers more control over flow rate, agitation, and percolation than most brewers and significantly reduces the possibility of channeling. This is achieved by a combination of elements, including the flat bottom and its form-fitting filter, which eliminate bypass, ensuring that all the liquid in the cup after the brew will contain coffee solids; the wide base (80mm in diameter) and vertical walls, which make for a shallow, even coffee bed that creates the ideal conditions for uniform water-coffee contact; and the dispersion screen, which distributes the water evenly, reducing the likelihood of channeling. The result of such a finely tuned brewing system is high extraction, which translates to the palate as dense flavor. 
 Agitation With Minimal Effort 
 An oft-overlooked aspect of pour-over brewing is the pour itself, which has the dual responsibility of evenly saturating and satisfactorily agitating the coffee grounds with the water. Although this sounds easy, it is not, and is most often helped along by a special gooseneck kettle and a steady hand. Tricolate, however, has removed that one variable from the equation. The precision holes in the Tricolate's dispersion screen control the flow rate, dictating how much water can get through at any given time, and the screen itself, mounted roughly four inches above the base, controls the pour height and therefore the agitation. As a result, it is possible to achieve consistently high extractions with minimal effort and with any kettle. All that is required for a perfect brew is the appropriate grind size and water temperature. The Tricolate will do the rest. 
 Environmentally Sound 
 The Tricolate is made in Australia of Tritan plastic, which is durable, heat-stable, and free from BPA, BPS, or other bisphenols. The German-made filters, a bag of which is included in the package, have a consistent pore structure, another reason for the high extractions, and, being relatively small, are made from less paper than those for traditional pour over brewers, reducing the environmental impact of every brew.

Name: Couverture Canephora - Pre-Order Now
Tasting_Notes: Chocolatey, berry-like, boozy, all in the same coffee?
Desc:
Fine Cup Award Winning Process  
 Exclusive Lot. Limited Edition: 16 kgs. 
 Chocolatey, berry-like, boozy, all in the same coffee? Yes, the complexity of this coffee is truly mind boggling! 
  This is the 3rd year of us bringing the Couverture Canephora to you. This beautiful Robusta is grown by Mr Mahesh Nayananan of TheNaturalFarmer, based in Pulneys, Tamil Nadu, and fermented using their proprietary methods.  
 Canephora, an old name of the Robusta, has us coming back for more. This coffee is fruity, acidic, and chocolatey - with zero bitterness, all at the same time! Tasting this coffee is like drinking a light and boozy Madagascar hot chocolate. Isn’t that mind-blowing? This coffee is a  limited lot of 16kg , and has won the Flavour of India - Fine Cup Award 2023 for Robusta Naturals. 
 We cupped the first edition of this coffee blind, with 5 people, and none of them could say it was a Robusta. It continues to blow many more minds ever since. 
 The coffee beans that go into Couverture Canephora were nurtured for 17 months - 12 months on the plant, 15 days for fermentation, and 4.5 months, for extended slow drying. The result of so much time, love, effort, and attention is something so complex, it opened our eyes.  Coming from sir Mahesh Narayanan and the team at TheNaturalFarmer, this coffee clearly reflects the excellent cultivation practices that the coffee has received during the harvest and beyond, from the nurturing of sapling to plant.

Name: Fiano Solaré - Roasted on 23/02
Tasting_Notes: florals once it cools down
Desc:
Citrusy, Orange Zest, Nuts, Almond, Caramel, Floral hints  
 Some choose therapists. But for some, coffee is the therapy.  No, not the just cup, but also the plants. Sujay Pradhan, the parent, as we'd like to call him, of this estate, treats this space as his  meditation retreat . Intercropping is essential for coffee, and Sujay didn't just handpick the coffee seeds, he also chose what he grew for shade. This estate is rich with  mango, lychee, cashew  ,  as well as  cardamom , amongst others. He has even put up signs next to the trees, for the visitors to enjoy. And yes, we asked - homestay coming soon! 
 Complex coffees with Orange Zest notes are a favourite, both in pour-overs, and espressos. We chose this lot for the notes, then made sure it was an omniroast. Processed by fermenting this coffee for 36 hours before washing it gives it complexity. It makes for a  smooth, enigmatic espresso , and a  complex pour-over  with slight  hints of florals  once it cools down. 
 This is our  first  offering from the  Koraput  region - a non-traditional area, and it comes from the Brown Valley Coffee Estate.  The Estate is one of the earliest  pioneers  of specialty-coffee processing in the Koraput valley. Established in 1993, it wasn’t an inheritance passed down through generations—it was a vision built from scratch. What was once an untouched valley was transformed by Sujay Pradhan into a thriving coffee estate, every plant sown with intention, care, and deliberation. 
 Young estates mean rich, fertile soil—and rich, dense coffee beans.  Espresso lovers , take note:  grind a touch coarser  to unlock the full depth of this cup. It makes extremely juicy, oily cups with those signature tiger stripes. It is forgiving in its grind sizes, but fine tuning improves taste and reduces bitterness significantly. We have learnt that grinding coarser works best for dense coffees such as this one.

Name: Garnet Vin Doux - Roasted on 04/03
Tasting_Notes: When brewed at 89°C for 2 1/2 mins using an AeroPress , the cup reveals a balanced, structured profile: Aromatics: Ferment-driven winey notes with subtle spice Flavor: Winey, D ark chocolate, prunes, and caramel sweetness.
Desc:
Grown along the outer slopes of the    Palani Hills at 4200 ft , this lot represents a precise approach to Robusta processing from    Ammikulavi Estate , Tamil Nadu. The estate spans 40 acres, where Arabicas occupy the central terrain and Robustas border the edges. 
 Under the direction of    Darshan , a sixth-generation grower and first-generation specialty processor, this coffee undergoes    anaerobic natural fermentation —a sealed environment that intensifies fruit complexity while refining mouthfeel and sweetness. 
 When brewed at    89°C  for  2 1/2 mins using an AeroPress , the cup reveals a balanced, structured profile: 
 
 
 Aromatics:    Ferment-driven winey notes with subtle spice 
 
 Flavor:   Winey, D ark chocolate, prunes, and caramel sweetness. 
 
 Body:    Full, syrupy texture with clean finish. 
 
 Acidity:    Low and integrated, enhancing perceived sweetness. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Taste Profile  -  Winey, Dark Chocolate,  Prunes, Caramel 
 
 
 
 Origin  -   Ammikulavi Estate, Pulneys, TN 
 
 
 
 Processing  - Anaerobic Naturals 
 
 
 
 Elevation  - 4200 ft 
 
 
 
   Roast:  Medium  Acidity:  Low  Sweetness:  Medium

Name: Good Afternoon - The Mid-Day Motivator
Desc:
After battling the morning hustle at the office, your nerves are rightly calling out for a cuppa. Replenish your diminishing energy (and patience, if we may add!) levels with a cup of our Afternoon blend, enough energy to wake you up, but not enough to disrupt your sleep at night. Did you say amazing? Yes, we know!   
 Made using hand-picked Washed Arabica from the SM Plantations, Koraput, Odisha for that chocolatey almond note with a caramel finish, and blended with the washed Robustas of the Rosegarden Farming Group for a mild bitter kick, this  70% Arabica and 30% Robusta  blend is designed to help you sail gracefully through the rest of your day. 
  So get this blend, and get ready for productive afternoons that will leave your coworkers awestruck!

Name: Prosecco Aventi - Pre-Order Now
Tasting_Notes: As it cools, a sweet pickled lemon brightness lifts through, tart but rounded, like a preserved citrus rather than a sharp acid.
Desc:
Taste Profile  -    Winy, Sweet Pickled Lemon, Malt 
 
 
 
 
 Origin  -   Koraput A1 Coffee Estate, Koraput, Odisha 
 
 
 
 Varietal -  Catimor 
 
 
 
 Processing  -          Extended Anaerobic Honey, 240 hrs sun-dried, Split beans 
 
 
 
 
 Elevation  - 3200 ft 
 
 
 
   
  Roast:  Medium  Acidity:  Bright  Sweetness:  High 
 From award-winning estate - Koraput A1 Estate 
   During harvest, unseasonal rainfall caused a portion of cherries to split — raising the very real risk of farmer losses. Rather than discard them, the lot was carefully segregated and given a second chance through one of the most labour-intensive processes in specialty coffee.     
 Each cherry was manually sorted, floated to remove defects, and sealed into fermentation vessels under oxygen-limited conditions for a full 240 hours — 10 days of controlled anaerobic fermentation, closely monitored to build aromatic complexity without tipping into over-fermentation.       
 Post-fermentation, the cherries were depulped with generous mucilage retained — the honey process — and moved to raised drying beds. Given the compromised skins, drying was managed with frequent turning to ensure even moisture migration. The parchment was then conditioned, rested, and dry-milled to grade.         
 Ten days of patience show up exactly where they should. The cup opens with a    winy depth    — that unmistakable ferment character that lingers on the sides of your tongue. As it cools, a    sweet pickled lemon    brightness lifts through, tart but rounded, like a preserved citrus rather than a sharp acid. The finish is long and grounding —    malt    warmth that settles everything into place. Best brewed slow. Best drunk without distraction.

Name: Robustas of Coorg - Roasted on 21/03
Tasting_Notes: chocolates, prunes, and raisins
Desc:
India is a land of smallholder farmers - and even coffee is grown at estates with less than a ton of production. And do you know what is the smallest quantity that can be graded and sorted in most affordable curing houses? A ton. So while we like the highest grade and best bean density in our coffee, the smallholders who do good work, don't get the limelight that they should, for the hard work they put in. Robusta is a healthy child that has adapted well to climate change, and is soon turning into the highlight of this industry, Worldwide.    
  Bhavika states that she had her biases against robusta - but this is the  first coffee  ever, that opened her mind to the possibilities that robusta holds in its folds. She believes it could be the first robusta for a lot of people, too!  
  The roasting, if Robusta conscious (credits to Rajeev Vaishnav), the sweetness and complexity in the bean can develop and shine. Name: Tawny Ristretta - Roasted on 04/03
Desc:
Limited edition of 45kg   Fine Robustas have always been close to our hearts, and this one adds yet another layer to our journey of discovering truly exceptional lots. 
 Hegbal Estate gets its name for   Hebbagillu -   Kannada for "great gateway". R un by Mr Devdas Menezes since 1996, he is a 3rd generational grower who has pioneered specialty harvests and post harvests for both Arabica and Robusta, and believes in a bright future for Robusta.  
 We got our hands on a beautiful bodied batch - an anaerobic Honey fermented twice for 60 hours. The cherries were stored in Ecotact bags, then pulped, and stored in Ecotact bags again.   After six months of experimentation and five distinct roast profiles, we’ve arrived at this expression — one that best highlights the character of this coffee. We’re releasing it in a limited batch at a special price to invite your palate into the conversation. Your feedback will shape how we take this coffee forward in future roasts.

Name: Classic Limited Edition Gift Box
Tasting_Notes: citrus & berries
Desc:
A premium gift box containing each of Microlot Coffees or the Estate Specialties. The best way to try out our products with your favorite brewing equipment during this festive season making it the ideal gifting option.  
    Micro-lot Coffees   
   Ice Cube   
  Selective harvest is done to ensure higher sugar content in the cherry. Post which, the cherries are washed with clean water and pulped. The coffee beans along with the mucilage are kept in extreme cold conditions to freeze the structure of the bean. The beans are then moved to raised drying beds and go through a slow and elongated drying process, thereby increasing the sweetness and imparting flavours of citrus & berries.  
  Banana Black Honey  
 When processing our Banana Black Honey at Harley Estate, we ensure to keep the maximum mucilage possible and is slowly dried under careful monitoring and a controlled environment with higher humidity, to achieve that elevated sweetness 
  Yellow Honey  
 Selective harvest done ensuring a higher sugar content in the cherry. These cherries are washed with clean water and undergo a unique process before being pulped. The coffee fruit is then pulped without the removal of the mucilage and is shade dried, thereby eventually attaining a yellow exterior & imparting sweet fruit notes, o ur Yellow Honey Coffee has notes of Cocoa, Toasted Hazelnut & Floral  
   
  Estate Specialties  
  Cardamom  
 We bring you a highly aromatic cardamom from Harley Estate. This special price, adds a lot of warmth to both sweet and savory dishes making it quintessentially Indian. Extra care is taken throughout the growing process and each pod is painstakingly harvested by hand. 
  Coffee Blossom Tea   
 Just for a few days in a year the estate is filled with an intoxicating perfume and endless white of the coffee blossoms. In this quick period, the flowers are individually hand picked, dried and cured. Bringing you the most delicate and heady floral tea, with notes of jasmine, oolong and vanilla. 
 Brewing Instructions : Add 2 or 3 grams of coffee blossom to 220ml of water (90-92 deg), let it steep for 2 mins, strain and enjoy. 
 Tastes great, hot or cold. 
  Cascara  
 Cascara which means "husk" or "peel" is the dried skin of coffee cherries. 
 At Harley Estate our Cascara is truly artisanal, we hand pulp the coffee cherries to retain juices of the cherry and increase the sweet fruitiness when the tea is brewed, our Cascara has hints of   Raw Mango, Lychee & Longan 
 Brewing Instructions : Add 2 or 3 grams of Cascara to 200ml of water (90-92 deg), let it steep for 2 mins, strain and enjoy hot, or on ice.

Name: Harley Estate Cascara
Tasting_Notes: Raw Mango, Lychee & Longan Brewing Instructions : Add 2 or 3 grams of Cascara to 200ml of water (90-92 deg), let it
Desc:
Cascara which means "husk" or "peel" is the dried skin of coffee cherries. 
 At Harley Estate our Cascara is truly artisanal, we hand pulp the coffee cherries to retain juices of the cherry and increase the sweet fruitiness when the tea is brewed, our Cascara has hints of  Raw Mango, Lychee & Longan  
 Brewing Instructions : Add 2 or 3 grams of Cascara to 200ml of water (90-92 deg), let it steep for 2 mins, strain and enjoy. 
 Qty : 50Gms

Name: Harley Estate Coffee Blossom Tea
Tasting_Notes: jasmine, oolong and vanilla
Desc:
Just for a few days in a year the estate is filled with an intoxicating perfume and endless white of the coffee blossoms. In this quick period, the flowers are individually hand picked, dried and cured. Bringing you the most delicate and heady floral tea, with notes of jasmine, oolong and vanilla. 
 Brewing Instructions : Add 2 or 3 grams of coffee blossom to 220ml of water (90-92 deg), let it steep for 2 mins, strain and enjoy. 
 Tastes great, hot or cold. 
  Arabica coffee blossom flowers from Harley Estate.

Tasting_Notes: The plantation consists of crops such as Coffee, Pepper, Cardamom, Cocoa, Bananas, Areca, Vanilla and Coconut.
Desc: Nestled within the Vast scape of the Western Ghats in India, is the Malnad region of Karnataka , with its rich heritage, Culture and abundance of some of India's best coffee plantations. Situated in Saklespur in the historic Munjarabad region, lies Harley Estate dating back to the early 1860's . The plantation consists of crops such as Coffee, Pepper, Cardamom, Cocoa, Bananas, Areca, Vanilla and Coconut. All crops are carefully planted in between natural and Jungle shade trees, with ecologically conscious farming practices, thereby preserving all the natural flora and fauna of the region.

Name: Culture Process
Desc: This exceptional coffee undergoes an 80-hour CULTURE PROCESS, sourced from the Catuai varietal at our farm, located 4,400 feet high in the Jeri Patte block. After harvesting with a Brix of 25.8, we placed the cherries in stainless-steel fermenters, adding a specific strain of yeast and lactic acid bacteria. The fermentation took place in a carbon dioxide-rich environment, followed by a slow drying process on raised beds over 29 days with constant stirring. This meticulous approach enhances the unique flavor profile of our coffee.

Name: Dark Room Naturals
Desc: This lot features a unique coffee processing method, starting with thermal shock applied to the cherries to enhance sugar readiness for fermentation. The cherries are then fermented for 48 hours with lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to ensure balanced acidity and optimal flavor development.  After fermentation, they are dried in a dark room for 12 days, minimizing UV degradation and preserving their complexity. The result is a coffee rich in flavor and exceptional quality.

Desc: During fermentation, we add petals to enhance flavor compounds, resulting in brighter fruit notes with floral characteristics. Name: Koji Robusta
Desc: The Koji process, is a vital fermentation technique used in East Asia This method involves inoculating steamed grains typically rice with Aspergillus oryzae spores which facilitate fermentation. Name: RC-7 Naturals
Desc: This is a 60-hour anaerobic fermentation natural processed coffee. It is from the Hemavathi varietal grown on our farm at 4450 feet from the block called Sivermara Patte. The Brix of the coffee cherries was 24.6 when harvested and they were put in the fermenters after floater removal. A strain of lab culture microbes were them introduced in a Nitrogen rich environment and allowed to ferment for 60 hours at 2.2 bar pressure. After removing the coffee from the fermenters, it was directly put on raised beds and dried for 29 days.

Name: ARABICA PEABERRY COFFEE
Tasting_Notes: At Devans, Arabica Peaberry is
Desc:
ANIMAL PRINTED PACKS AVAILABLE IN 500 g ONLY 
  Indian coffees are home to the best shade grown coffees in the world. It grows Arabica and Robusta coffees in the southern states where lush coffee plantations are heavily inter cropped with black pepper and ginger that bustle with honeybees and yield the finest coffee beans.  
  Peaberry coffees are rare, comprising only 3-7% of the total crop. These pea-shaped, natural formations of the coffee bean are thought to form when several pistils get knocked off the coffee flower, causing only one seed to form inside the coffee fruit rather than two.  
  Normally coffee beans grow two to a cherry, flat against each other but in about five percent of the worlds coffee a bean is found to be solo that's Peaberry.  
  Because there's no way to tell from looking at the cherry whether there's a single or double bean inside, as a result Peaberry beans are hand picked and processed to be enjoyed separately.  
 Tasting notes:    
  At Devans, Arabica Peaberry is roasted in a way to create a mild strength of coffee, that is soft, smooth, highly aromatic and flavorful . If you like milder coffees, go for this lighter bodied and a clean cup of coffee. It’s ideal when made in a French Press or a pour over.

Name: ARABICA PEABERRY DARK ROAST COFFEE
Tasting_Notes: Floral aroma, bright medium to full bodied coffee, completely void of acidity, with a chocolaty finish and dark color in the cup
Desc:
ANIMAL PRINTED PACKS AVAILABLE IN 500 g ONLY.  
   Baba Budangiri, is home to the finest coffee plantations of India. Indian Arabica Peaberry is a hand-selected, pulped, and fully washed coffee. Separating the peaberries from the rest of the coffee beans requires the use of special screens and adds time and effort to the grading process. The resulting peaberry coffee is very dense and uniform, resulting in a very focused and consistent flavor.

  Tasting Notes  
  Floral aroma, bright medium to full bodied coffee, completely void of acidity, with a chocolaty finish and dark color in the cup.

Name: ASSAM CLASSIC TEA (Granular)
Tasting_Notes: This tea is CTC Assam, only for those who enjoy a rich, dark liquor and malty flavor.
Desc:
Assam CTC Classic Tea   
 Black Tea Summer Harvest 2025.  
 The second flush Assam CTC is regarded as the best CTC tea in the world.    
  CTC means the tea has been processed in a " Cut, Tear, and Curl" machine. Tea leaves are shoved in the top, totally destroyed and then reformed into pellets. These pellets turn brown (oxidize ) very quickly. This makes for the super-brisk tea.  
 This tea is CTC Assam, only for those who enjoy a rich, dark liquor and malty flavor. It's best when boiled with milk.

There is a hint of floral fruitiness that reveals itself, with subtle notes of citrus around the edges. The lingering sweetness towards the end stays with you for quite some time.

Desc:

  Djimmah is grown in the Illubabor and Kaffa regions of Ethiopia at elevations from 4,400 to 6,000 feet above sea level within the biggest catchment area in Ethiopia, an area that produces and exports about 60,000 tons of coffee each year. Djimmah is also called Jimma Coffee. A unique coffee thought to be the variety closest in flavour to the original wild plant. This is an ideal climate and the plants are well protected by the larger forest trees which provide shade from the midday sun and preserve the moisture in the soil.   
  Coffee from Ethiopia is known for its bright fruited and floral flavours. These coffees typically have a higher acidity, light to medium body and complex flavour notes.

Matcha is finely ground powder of specially grown and processed green tea leaves, traditionally consumed in East Asia. The green tea plants used for matcha are shade-grown for three to four weeks before harvest and the stems and veins are removed during processing.   
  This is all natural, pure, gluten-free and vegan.  
  Matcha tea, unique to Japan is a finely ground powder of green tea leaves.   Loaded with antioxidants, it’s health benefits are unparalleled. With a rich and vibrant green colour, the dry matcha powder is deeply aromatic and gives off an earthy aroma of fresh mountainous spring greens.

Name: MONSOONED MALABAR - ARABICA AA
Tasting_Notes: Monsooned flavor, low on acidity, mellow taste and a golden color in the cup
Desc:
ANIMAL PRINTED PACKS AVAILABLE IN 500 g ONLY. 
  Monsooned Malabar AA pure arabica, is a specialty coffee of India and one of the world's most sought after Indian coffee beans. These exotic beans undergo a unique process, beans are cured only on the Malabar coast during the south-west monsoon months of June to September that results in producing their amazing flavor profile. Sun dried green beans are warehoused only on the Malabar coast, in the west coast of India, where deliberate exposure to the sea air and monsoon winds result in the beans to swell, fade and reduce acidity.  
  Tasting Notes  
  Monsooned flavor, low on acidity, mellow taste and a golden color in the cup. Medium roasted to bring out notes of spice, mustiness, wood, chocolate and nuts. It has a sweetish finish, adding very rich crema to espresso cup.

Name: NILGIRI TEA  (Whole Leaf Tea FOP grade)
Tasting_Notes: Nilgiri tea is variously described as being light but full-bodied or well-rounded in flavour, with fruit, like citrus, and floral notes.
Desc:
A strong Single origin leaf tea from the blue mountains - Nilgiri Tea   
  The Nilgiri Mountains form the border between the southern states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, but are predominately within the District of Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu. Also called the blue mountain tea, this Nilgiri black tea is stronger in the cup than Darjeeling and Assam.    Nilgiri tea is variously described as being light but full-bodied or well-rounded in flavour, with fruit, like citrus, and floral notes.  
  Single origin leaf tea when brewed, is dark colour in the cup, intensely aromatic, with lively fragrant flavours, a quality attributed to its climatic growing conditions.

Name: ROOIBOS TEA
Tasting_Notes: A properly brewed cup of rooibos tea will be a rich red color and have a sweet, nutty flavour.
Desc:
Rooibos tea is made from the leaves of "red bush" plant, which grows only in the small Cederberg region of South Africa. Because it does not derive from the Camillia sinensis plant (like black, white, green or oolong teas), rooibos tea is considered more of an herbal drink or tisane than a "true" tea. Rooibos tea is often called "red tea" or "red bush" tea because of the bright red coloring the leaves take on during the oxidation and fermentation processes. A properly brewed cup of rooibos tea will be a rich red color and have a sweet, nutty flavour.   
 Net weight: 50 g

Name: CRIMSON SPIRIT - Pineapple Ferment - Kalyancool Estate (In-House)
Tasting_Notes: strawberry and plum emerge, finishing with a whiskey-like boozy warmth that lingers beautifully
Desc:
Kalyancool Pineapple Fermentation – Crimson Spirit   
 This is the best microlot we have roasted in last 365 days.. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:   Light Plus  
  100% Arabica   
 Rooted in our own estate at Kalyancool, this experimental microlot celebrates precision fermentation and fruit-forward innovation. Crafted from  350 kg of fully ripened red cherries , this lot undergoes an  anaerobic natural fermentation  enhanced with  75 kg of fresh pineapple , carefully integrated with a  developed yeast strain  to guide flavor clarity and intensity. 
 Fermented for  72 hours  with the fruit intact, this process unlocks a bold tropical expression while preserving balance and structure. The cup opens with an unmistakable  pineapple candy sweetness , juicy and playful, followed by layers of  jackfruit and ripe mango richness . As it cools, elegant hints of  strawberry and plum  emerge, finishing with a  whiskey-like boozy warmth  that lingers beautifully. 
 This is a confident, expressive coffee—crafted to stand out, not blend in. 
 📍  Estate:  Kalyancool Estate, Chikmagalur 🌿  Process:  Anaerobic Naturals with Pineapple 🍍  Fruit Ratio:  350 kg coffee cherries : 75 kg pineapple 🕒  Fermentation:  72 hours 🌱  Yeast:  Developed estate yeast strain 🔥  Roast:  Light Plus 
 Varietal: Chandragiri, Selection 795 
  Tasting Notes:  🍍 Pineapple Candy 🍈 Jackfruit 🥭 Mango 🍓 Strawberry 🍑 Plum 🥃 Whiskey-like Booziness 
 Experience Kalyancool Pineapple Fermentation—a vibrant, fruit-driven microlot where tropical sweetness meets controlled fermentation artistry. 
  Resting Period:  Minimum  10 days

Name: Everyday Gold – Affordable Value | Auto Discounted | No Codes
Tasting_Notes: Toasted Almond • Golden Raisin • Milk Chocolate A clean, balanced cup with elegant sweetness
Desc:
Everyday Gold Value 
  Premium taste. Practical price.  
 Crafted for daily brewers who don’t want to compromise,  Everyday Gold Value  is a washed roast made from carefully hand-sorted B-sized Arabica beans grown on our own estate in Chikmagalur. Though slightly smaller in size, these beans are upgraded to specialty grade through meticulous post-harvest sorting. Fully washed and given a 10-hour water drain, this coffee ensures clarity, consistency, and a smooth daily cup. 
 Resting Period: 
 Medium Roast Profile: 14 days from roast date.  
 Dark Minus Roast Profile: 5 days from roast date.  
 💡  Now available in two roast levels — customers can select their preferred option (Medium or Medium Dark) while placing the order.  
 Both roast profiles are crafted with purpose — the Medium Roast is a filter roast, ideal for manual brewing methods for black. It offers juicy acidity with minimum bitterness, perfect for clean black brews. The Dark Minus Roast, though developed as an espresso roast, also performs beautifully on manual brewing equipment, giving a full-bodied cup with rich chocolate depth that pairs wonderfully with milk or stands strong on its own. 
 
 Medium Roast ☕ 
  Tasting Notes:  Toasted Almond • Golden Raisin • Milk Chocolate A clean, balanced cup with elegant sweetness. Perfect for those who enjoy  bright, smooth flavors  in both black and milk-based brews. 
 
 Dark MINUS Roast ☕ 
  Tasting Notes:  Cocoa • Roasted Hazelnut • Caramelized Date • Brown Sugar A deeper, fuller-bodied cup with  rich chocolate depth  and nutty-sweet complexity. Ideal for those who love a  comforting, bold brew  that pairs beautifully with milk. 
 
 🌱  100% Arabica | Single-Estate (Aldur, Chikmagalur)  💧  Washed Process (10-hour drain)  🧺  Hand-sorted, uniform medium-sized beans  🔥  Available in Medium & Medium Dark Roasts (selectable option)  📦  Whole Bean & Ground Options

 This is a beautifully balanced microlot from  Ratnagiri Estate , showcasing how terroir-driven fermentation can produce deep sweetness and layered fruit complexity while maintaining clarity in the cup. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  100% Arabica  
 Sourced from a  single lot at Ratnagiri Estate , this coffee is crafted from carefully harvested ripe cherries with a  Brix level of 23.8 , indicating excellent fruit maturity and sugar development. 
 The cherries come from  Block 5/1 of the 17 Acres Patte section , planted with the  Catuai varietal , known for its clean structure and ability to express terroir-driven sweetness. 
 After harvest, only the ripest cherries are selected and the floaters are removed. The cherries are then transferred into  bio-fermenters where they undergo a controlled 48-hour anaerobic fermentation using native terroir microbes naturally present on the fruit . This process allows the estate’s unique microbial environment to shape the flavor development of the coffee. 
 Following fermentation, the cherries are dried slowly on  raised beds for approximately 29 days , completing the process as a  natural coffee . The slow drying stabilizes the sugars and enhances the development of caramel-like sweetness and fruit complexity. 
 The beans are then roasted  Light Plus , preserving the coffee’s natural sweetness and aromatic structure. 
 The cup opens with a  rich brown sugar sweetness , smooth and caramel-like, forming the foundation of the profile. This is followed by subtle layers of  mulberry, grapes, and guava , adding gentle fruit complexity. As the coffee cools, softer notes of  banana and delicate black tea  appear, bringing a refined, elegant finish with a lingering sweetness. 
 This is a terroir-focused coffee that highlights how  native microbial fermentation and slow natural drying can produce a clean yet deeply sweet cup.

Name: THERMAL SHOCK -  Ruby Pulse - Kalyancool Estate (In-House)
Tasting_Notes: 🍉 Watermelon 🍷 Grape Wine 🍎 Pomegranate 🍇 Dried Grapes 🍑 Prunes Experience Thermal Shock - Ruby Pulse —a striking experimental microlot where extreme temperature contrast, bruised natural
Desc:
Kalyancool Thermal Shock Fermentation – Ruby Pulse  
 This is one of the most technically experimental microlots we have produced this year—an expressive coffee that demonstrates how extreme temperature contrast and controlled fermentation can unlock deep fruit complexity and wine-like character. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  100% Arabica  
 Rooted in our own estate at  Kalyancool , this microlot explores the effect of  thermal shock processing combined with controlled yeast fermentation . Carefully selected fully ripened red cherries are first sorted to remove floaters and underripe fruits, ensuring only dense, high-quality cherries enter the process. 
 The cherries are then subjected to a  thermal shock treatment , where they are immersed in  55°C warm water for 5 minutes . This controlled heat exposure helps soften the fruit structure and prepares the cherries for rapid cellular stress. Immediately after heating, the cherries are transferred to  ice chamber and rapidly chilled , remaining in the cold bath for around  7–8 minutes . 
 This dramatic temperature contrast creates a “thermal shock” effect that enhances permeability of the fruit and intensifies the interaction between sugars, microbes, and yeast during fermentation. 
 After the thermal treatment, the cherries are gently  bruised to create a bruised natural process , allowing partial opening of the fruit skin while maintaining the natural mucilage and pulp around the beans. 
 The cherries are then inoculated with  activated Lalcafe Intenso yeast , a strain chosen for its ability to enhance fruity aromatics and wine-like complexity. Fermentation takes place in  sealed Eco-tact bags for 72 hours , allowing controlled anaerobic conditions to develop layered fruit character. 
 Once fermentation is complete, the coffee is dried as naturals and carefully  light (light plus) roasted  to preserve clarity, acidity, and aromatic intensity. 
 The cup opens with  fresh watermelon sweetness , juicy and refreshing. This is followed by vibrant  pomegranate acidity , adding brightness and structure. As the coffee develops on the palate, deeper  grape-wine notes emerge , bringing a rich fermented fruit character. As the cup cools, darker fruit layers of  prunes and dried grapes  appear, creating a long, wine-like finish with lingering sweetness. 
 This is a bold experimental coffee designed to showcase how  thermal shock processing and precision fermentation can transform natural coffees into intensely fruit-driven microlots.  
 📍  Estate:  Kalyancool Estate, Chikmagalur 🌿  Process:  Thermal Shock Bruised Natural 🌡  Thermal Shock Step:  55°C warm water → immediate ice bath 🕒  Fermentation:  72 hours anaerobic fermentation 🌱  Yeast:  Lalcafe Intenso 🔥  Roast:  Light 
  Varietal:  Chandragiri, Selection 795 
 Tasting Notes 
 🍉 Watermelon 🍷 Grape Wine 🍎 Pomegranate 🍇 Dried Grapes 🍑 Prunes

Udaygiri Estate Whisky Barrel Aged – Oak Reserve  
 This is one of the most refined barrel-aged coffees we have roasted this year—an elegant microlot where specialty coffee meets the depth and character of whisky oak maturation. 
 ☕  Roast Profile Available:  Light Plus 
  100% Arabica  
 Sourced from  Udaygiri Estate in Chikmagalur , this microlot explores how oak maturation can enhance coffee complexity while preserving clarity and fruit structure. 
 Carefully selected ripe cherries are processed as naturals and dried to the ideal moisture level. Once stabilized, the green beans are transferred into  seasoned whisky barrels  that previously held aged whisky. The beans are then  rested inside the barrels for several weeks , allowing the porous green coffee to slowly absorb the aromatic compounds embedded in the oak. 
 During this maturation period, the beans take on subtle layers of  oak wood tannins, vanilla sweetness, and whisky-like aromatic complexity , while still preserving the natural fruit character of the coffee. 
 Once the desired infusion is achieved, the beans are removed and roasted  Light Plus , ensuring the barrel characteristics remain elegant and integrated rather than overpowering. 
 The cup opens with crisp  green apple acidity , bright and refreshing. This is followed by juicy layers of  kiwi, grapes, and stone fruits , adding a lively fruit sweetness that balances the barrel influence. As the coffee develops, the profile deepens into rich  whisky-like warmth , supported by pronounced  oakwood structure  and delicate  vanilla undertones  that linger into the finish. 
 This is a sophisticated coffee that highlights how  barrel aging can complement specialty coffee without overshadowing its natural fruit profile.

Desc:

   Suitable for all brew methods.

  Characteristics  
 
   Sweet, vibrant cup with bright acidity, a medium-heavy body & lingering sweetness.   
 
 
 
  Minimum resting period  
   Filter 6 Days | Espresso 14 Days   
 
 
  A song that pairs well  
    
 
 
 
   
  About the region / estate :   
 This lot was sourced from  St. Joseph Estate , situated in the hills of  Perumalmalai in Kodaikanal , a region often referred to as the  Princess of Hill Stations . The estate sits at approximately  4000 feet above sea level , where cooler mountain temperatures allow for slower cherry maturation and a more concentrated sugar development in the fruit. 
 The coffee is composed of  Catimore, Chandragiri, and SLN9  cultivars, varieties well suited to the high elevation conditions of the region. Cherries were harvested at peak ripeness and processed as  sun-dried naturals , using  controlled dehydrator technology  to carefully regulate moisture loss during the drying phase. This method allows for a stable fermentation environment while preserving the integrity of the fruit sugars and aromatic compounds. 
  Roasters thought :  
 During roasting, we aimed to highlight the coffee’s  natural fruit density and creamy structure . The profile follows a  light roast approach with elevated airflow and a development ratio of approximately 14% , allowing for clarity of flavour while maintaining the underlying sweetness and tactile body. 
 In the cup, the coffee expresses a profile reminiscent of  strawberries and cream , supported by a soft  mandarin-like acidity  and layered tropical fruit undertones. The acidity is  sweet and rounded rather than sharp , and the mouthfeel develops into a  medium to medium-heavy body with a smooth, almost velvety texture . 
 
  Roast Profile:  
 Sample Roast Machine : Bullet IBTS R1 
 Roast Machine : Probat VFD 
  Development % : 14 First Crack Temperature : Below 194 °  Celsius    
  Brew Approach:  
 19 GMS Med-Fine (Fellow Ode Gen 2.0, 3.9 Setting) 55 ML bloom 45 seconds  Swirl immediately after pour Then 80 ML Then At 1.30 again 80 ML Then again 95 ML to finish it off with gentle swirl in the end.  
 Water at 97  °  Celsius (TDS not more than 140 PPM).

    Roaster thoughts :     Fermented naturals from ratnagiri estate profiled as an ultra light to bring out the floral notes from this LOT. This coffee is one the most unique single origin coffees's we have come across. A lot that everyone must try to understand terror and complexity Indian specialty coffee can deliver. It was a challenge at first to understand the nature, origin and process of this LOT, but as we sample roasted and cupped first few batches we knew where we were headed. Clean floral aromatics, jasmine in your final cup & bright acidity makes this a very enjoyable cup of coffee.   
   Brewing   Note:      Due   to   its   delicate   roast   level,   we   recommend   brewing   this   coffee   with    higher   water   temperatures (97°  C)      and   a   controlled   pour   to   ensure   full   extraction.   Attention   to    grind   size,   agitation,   and   brew   time      is   critical   to   achieve   optimal   clarity   and   balance   in   the   cup.  
  This   coffee   is   a   testament   to   our   commitment   to   innovation   and   continuous   refinement   in   roasting.   
 
 
 The estate and efforts:     We all are familiar with the producer Mr. Ashok Patre and his family run estate Ratnagiri Estate. Our founder visited the farm back in the month of march 2021 when coffee processing was at its peak.   A day's visit to the estate to understand the farm, the processing techniques and the history behind the legacy was great. Our meeting began with knowing each other and talking and about the passion that runs Grey Soul Coffee as a brand.   Then it led to discussions about the specialty community and culture in our country right now. Moving on, we spoke about cup score, Q grading and how it varies from person to person and hence become highly subjective.   Then we spoke about international markets and a comparison between Indian and south American coffee. Then quickly moved on a long elaborate your of the farm where some coffee was milled and ready, some drying on raised beds, some drying out in the fields and hand garbling in works as final sorting was in process.   In the end, specialty coffee can be simply defined as the coffee that is of the best quality without comprises. This is exactly what this estate stands for and believes in.

 Minimum rest (Filter): 10 days after roast date Minimum rest (Espresso): Up to 3 weeks after roast date

Name: 5AM Club
Tasting_Notes: A nutty, almondy warmth that hits like the quiet after chaos - you know, that breath of stillness before the next sunrise.
Desc:
Chocolate that means business. Caramel that gives a nod, not a grin. A nutty, almondy warmth that hits like the quiet after chaos - you know, that breath of stillness before the next sunrise. Whether you're the last one standing after the party or the first one chasing the day, this is your rallying sip.

   PROCESSING:  Monsooning + Washed 
  REGION:  Chikmagalur 
  ALTITUDE:  1100 MASL (metres above sea level) 
  VARIETAL:  SL9 
  Where the 5 AM Club Begins  In the quiet of Anoor village in Tamil Nadu, where the mornings are misty and time feels unhurried, sits Hoysala Estate. Named after the ancient dynasty that once ruled this land, the estate has stood its ground since the late 1800s, tended by the same family for four generations. 
 Here, at elevations at 1100 MASL (metres above sea level), coffee grows in rhythm with the land. Intercropped with cardamom, the plants mature under a canopy of care and patience. It’s not just where the 5 AM Club is grown. It’s where it’s born: steady, grounded, and ready for the day.   
  HARVEST:  2025 
  BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual 
  BEVERAGE STYLE:  W/Milk

Name: Golden Hour
Tasting_Notes: that one rare moment you actually pause - mid-scroll, mid-chaos - when the sunlight spills in and for no reason at all, you smile
Desc:
Like a soft spotlight through the blinds - orange zest, stone fruit, and juicy apple line up for their solo. It's plum, but polished. This cup? It tastes like that one rare moment you actually pause - mid-scroll, mid-chaos - when the sunlight spills in and for no reason at all, you smile. Just for existing. It’s your reminder: reset the clock.  
  ROAST LEVEL:  Medium Light 
   PROCESSING:  Washed 
  REGION:  Hoyasala Estate (  Tamil Nadu ) &  The Laks Farm(Tamil Nadu) 
  ALTITUDE:  1300 MASL (metres above sea level) 
  VARIETAL:  SL9 
  HARVEST:  2025 
  BEST BREW METHOD:  Expresso & Manual (French Press, Aeropress, Pour-over, Channi style, South Indian Filter) 
  BEVERAGE STYLE:  Manual Brew, Milk Based Drinks  
  Where Golden Hour Grows  Golden Hour is born where stillness meets intention - on two farms that honour the land, the craft, and the quiet magic of doing things the right way. 
 In the Pulney Hills of Tamil Nadu, you’ll find The Laks Farm in Pachalur village. One of the highest coffee-growing regions in India, it's a place where biodiversity thrives, coffee trees growing alongside oranges, bananas, cardamom, and pepper. Everything here is organic, intentional, and deeply alive. The result? Coffees that are bright, layered, and lingering like light catching the edge of the day. 
 Down south in Anoor village, Hoysala Estate carries the weight of history, named after a dynasty that once ruled this very soil. The estate has been family-run since the late 1800s, with a quiet focus on growing coffee that speaks for itself. At 1100 meters, intercropped with cardamom and processed with care - natural, washed, honey, and even monsooned, their approach is steady, patient, and precise. 
 Together, these two farms create something balanced and beautiful. Golden Hour is a blend full of grace and is soft, rounded, and golden in every sense.
